text.p: --BIRTHDAYS--
French composer CHARLES CAMILLE SAINT-SAENS was born in 1835. He wrote "Samson And Delilah" and "Danse Macabre".
French Jewish army officer ALFRED DREYFUS was born in 1859. He was wrongly imprisoned for treason with false evidence on Devil's Island. He was exonerated after a public investigation.
French actor, film director and screenwriter JACQUES TATI was born in 1908.

Former Beatle JOHN LENNON was born in 1940. The English pop singer, musician and songwriter rose to fame with the "Fab Four" and later, after the band's break-up in 1969, formed the Plastic Ono Band with his wife YOKO ONO. His 1969 "Give Peace A Chance" became the anthem for the peace movement. His solo work alternated between the confessional and the political. Hits included "Imagine" (1971), "Happy Christmas" (1972), "Whatever Gets You Through The Night" (1974), "Woman" (1981) and "Nobody Told Me" (1984). He was shot dead by a fan on the 8th December, 1980.

United State singer, guitarist, pianist and songwriter JACKSON BROWNE was born in Heidelberg in 1948. He started as a guitarist with the Nitty Gritty Dirt Band and was successful as a songwriter for performers such as TOM RUSH, LINDA RONSTADT and The Eagles. Solo hits included "Running On Empty" (1978), "Somebody's Baby" (1982) and "Lawyers In Love" (1983).
British middle-distance runner STEVE OVETT, who won a gold medal at the Moscow Olympics in 1980, was born in 1955.
--EVENTS--
1192 : King RICHARD the Lion Heart abandoned the Holy
Land after an unsuccessful crusade, leaving Jerusalem in Muslim hands.
1933 : The Australian Cricket Board was assured by the
Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) that the controversial practice of bodyline bowling would not be used in England the following year.
1939 : The Prices of Food Bill was introduced in London
to control profiteering.
1944 : The decision to form the United Nations was made.
The new world-wide organisation was set up to preserve peace after the end of World War II.
1947 : The Australian federal opposition called for a
royal commission into the activities of communists.
1959 : MARGARET THATCHER was elected to parliament as a
Tory MP.
1962 : Uganda received independence.
1963 : Three thousand lives were lost when the Vaiont Dam
in the Italian Alps was wrecked by a rock slide.
1973 : ELVIS PRESLEY divorced his wife PRISCILLA.
1974 : Bankcard was introduced in Australia. A day later
major department stores in Melbourne rejected the cards.
1987 : At the conservatives' conference, MARGARET

THATCHER told the delegates she wanted at least another seven years as leader. Three years later splits in the party over the issues of Europe and consensus government forced her resignation. She was Prime Minister from 1979 to 1990.
1989 : Asian immigration to Australia rose by 11.5
percent from 1988 to 1989.
